In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is a powerful tool that can be used to predict protein function in various biological contexts, and it outperforms existing methods in most cases.
the joint embedding of amino acid sequence and protein protein interaction network data outperforms the embedding of each of them individually.
our approach outperforms the existing state-of-the-art methods for tissue specific protein function annotation on 10 out 13 tissues by an average of 19%.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new computational method that can learn joint representations of protein function from both amino acid sequences and protein protein interactions.
we have shown that protein function is not only an emergent property at the protein level, but also at the level of protein protein interactions.
we learn joint representations of proteins by combining sequence and multilayers protein protein interaction networks that are more effective in predicting protein function than existing methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
by combining sequence and network information, one can improve the performance on a downstream prediction task.
by combining information at multiple levels of abstraction, we can improve the accuracy of function prediction.
by learning representations that integrate information from both sequence and networks, we can improve protein function prediction.
